question: According to the Reserve Bank of India, as of October 2024, India became the fourth country whose foreign exchange (forex) reserves swelled to $_______ billion.
solution:
The correct answer is __**701**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of October 2024, India became the fourth country in the world to have foreign exchange (forex) reserves exceeding **$701 billion**.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is responsible for managing the country’s forex reserves, which include foreign currency assets, gold reserves, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and the reserve position in the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
 
• India’s forex reserves crossed the $700 billion mark, highlighting its strong economic fundamentals and resilience in the global financial landscape.
 
• Other countries with similar high forex reserves include China, Japan, and Switzerland.
 
• Maintaining high forex reserves is essential for stabilizing the Indian rupee and supporting India’s imports, external debt, and economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves**

 
 
• Forex reserves consist of foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs (Special Drawing Rights), and the reserve position in the IMF.
 
• These reserves act as a buffer against external economic shocks and ensure financial stability.
 
• They are critical for maintaining investor confidence and supporting the balance of payments.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**
 
 
• The RBI is India’s central bank, tasked with managing monetary policy, regulating banks, and overseeing the country’s forex reserves.
 
• It actively intervenes in the forex market to stabilize the Indian rupee against global currencies.
 
 
 
• **Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)**
 
 
• SDRs are supplementary foreign exchange reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
 
• They are based on a basket of major international currencies, including the US dollar, euro, yuan, yen, and pound sterling.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Forex Reserves**
 
 
• They enable a country to meet its external obligations, including import payments and debt repayments.
 
• High reserves help mitigate currency volatility and ensure economic stability during global financial crises.
 
 
 
• **India’s Forex History**
 
 
• India’s forex reserves have grown significantly since the economic liberalization of 1991, when they were critically low.
 
• In 2021, India’s forex reserves exceeded $600 billion for the first time, showcasing its economic progress.
